
```{r}
###############################################################################
# Extract raw RNA-seq counts for 4 patient-derived organoids (PDOs)
#   BO-046, BO-114, BO-189, BO-268
#
# PURPOSE
#   This script pulls the raw counts of the
#   four PDOs out of the organoid RNA-seq count matrix, checks them, and saves
#   a clean gene x sample matrix. That matrix is the input for the next step:
#   one joint VST run (PDOs + pILC tumors), then ssGSEA (Hallmark).
#
# INPUT (organoid RNA-seq data, Michael Gorry)
#   Org_RAWcounts__ENSG_63140.csv      raw counts, Ensembl IDs (used here)
#   colData_organoid_metadata.xlsx     sample metadata (used for checking only)
#   Not used here: Org_RNAseq_RAWcounts_IDconverted_63140.csv (symbol version)
#
# KNOWN FEATURES OF THE COUNT FILE (found while testing)
#   1. Row 1 is a SECOND header (featureCounts style): "Geneid" followed by the
#      BAM path of each sample. Because of this, R reads every column as text.
#      The script removes this row and keeps the BAM paths as a record.
#   2. Ensembl IDs carry version numbers (e.g. ENSG00000290825.1). They are
#      kept here; remove them later with sub("\\..*$", "", id), as in the pILC
#      DESeq2/ssGSEA script.
#   3. The BAM name of BO-268 is "BO268_S36_B...". The extra "B" may mean a
#      second library, a re-sequencing run or a batch. Check the metadata.
#
# OUTPUT (folder: OUT, no dates in file names)
#   PDO_raw_counts.csv            gene x 4 samples, raw integer counts
#   PDO_sample_to_bam_map.csv     which BAM file each sample came from
#   PDO_library_sizes.csv         total counts per sample (quality check)
#   (the metadata rows of the 4 samples are only printed to the console)
#
# SAFETY CHECKS (the script stops with an error if any of them fails)
#   - each sample name matches exactly one column
#   - the BAM path in row 1 contains the same sample ID (cross-check)
#   - after removing the header row, no value is lost by number conversion
#   - all values are whole numbers and not negative (true raw counts)
#   - gene IDs are unique
#
# NEXT STEP
#   Merge these counts with the pILC tumor counts (4_Count_file_pILC) on shared
#   protein-coding genes, run vst(blind = TRUE) ONCE on all samples, then run
#   ssGSEA (Hallmark) on the joint VST matrix.
###############################################################################

suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(readxl)
})

SEED <- 42
set.seed(SEED)

# ------------------------------- 1. PATHS ------------------------------------
IN_DIR   <- "/ix1/alee/LO_LAB/Personal/Michael_Gorry/Org_RNAseq_Data"
COUNTS   <- file.path(IN_DIR, "Org_RAWcounts__ENSG_63140.csv")
METADATA <- file.path(IN_DIR, "colData_organoid_metadata.xlsx")

OUT <- "/ix1/alee/LO_LAB/Personal/Rahul/pILC/RNASeq/PDO"
dir.create(OUT, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

want <- c("BO-046", "BO-114", "BO-189", "BO-268")   # samples to extract

# Helper: make names comparable (ignore case, dots, hyphens, underscores)
# "BO-046", "BO046" and "bo_046" all become "BO046"
key <- function(x) toupper(gsub("[^A-Za-z0-9]", "", x))

# --------------------------- 2. READ COUNT MATRIX ----------------------------
# check.names = FALSE keeps the original column names
# colClasses = "character": read everything as text first, so that the extra
# header row cannot silently change the column types; we convert below
cnt <- read.csv(COUNTS, check.names = FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE,
                colClasses = "character")
cat("Count file dimensions (rows x columns):", dim(cnt), "\n")
cat("First column names:", paste(head(colnames(cnt), 10), collapse = ", "), "\n")

# ----------------------- 3. MATCH THE 4 SAMPLE NAMES -------------------------
# Search each sample ID in the column names (column 1 = gene IDs is skipped)
sample_cols <- colnames(cnt)[-1]
hit <- lapply(want, function(w) which(grepl(key(w), key(sample_cols), fixed = TRUE)) + 1L)
names(hit) <- want
print(hit)   # each sample must match exactly one column

n_hit <- lengths(hit)
if (any(n_hit != 1))
  stop("These samples do not match exactly one column: ",
       paste(names(n_hit)[n_hit != 1], collapse = ", "),
       "\nLook at the column names printed above (e.g. 'BO046', '_S12' suffix).")

sel <- cnt[, c(1, unlist(hit))]
colnames(sel) <- c("gene", want)

# ------------------ 4. REMOVE THE SECOND HEADER ROW (BAM PATHS) --------------
# Row 1 = "Geneid" + BAM paths (featureCounts style). Keep it as a record.
stopifnot(sel$gene[1] == "Geneid")
bam_paths <- unlist(sel[1, want])

# Cross-check: the sample ID must also appear in its own BAM path
ok <- mapply(function(w, b) grepl(key(w), key(b), fixed = TRUE), want, bam_paths)
if (!all(ok))
  stop("Column name and BAM path disagree for: ", paste(want[!ok], collapse = ", "))

sel <- sel[-1, ]
rownames(sel) <- NULL

# ---------------------------- 5. CONVERT AND CHECK ---------------------------
# Convert to numbers. NAs created here would mean text values were lost,
# so we check for that right after.
sel[want] <- lapply(sel[want], function(v) as.numeric(trimws(v)))

stopifnot(!anyNA(sel[want]))                                  # nothing lost
m <- as.matrix(sel[want])
stopifnot(all(abs(m - round(m)) < 1e-8))                      # whole numbers
stopifnot(all(m >= 0))                                        # no negatives
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(sel$gene))                           # unique gene IDs
stopifnot(all(grepl("^ENSG", sel$gene)))                      # all Ensembl IDs
sel[want] <- lapply(sel[want], as.integer)                    # raw integer counts

# Library sizes: the four samples should be in a similar range
lib <- data.frame(sample = want,
                  total_counts = colSums(sel[want]),
                  genes_with_counts = colSums(sel[want] > 0),
                  row.names = NULL)
print(lib)

# ----------------------------- 6. METADATA CHECK -----------------------------
# Print the metadata rows that mention the 4 samples (what does "_B" mean for
# BO-268? batch? re-sequencing?). Console output only; nothing is saved.
meta <- read_excel(METADATA)
cat("\nMetadata columns:", paste(colnames(meta), collapse = ", "), "\n")

row_has_sample <- apply(meta, 1, function(r)
  any(sapply(want, function(w) any(grepl(key(w), key(as.character(r)), fixed = TRUE)))))
meta_sub <- meta[row_has_sample, , drop = FALSE]
print(as.data.frame(meta_sub))

# ------------------------------- 7. SAVE OUTPUTS -----------------------------
write.csv(sel, file.path(OUT, "PDO_raw_counts.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(data.frame(sample = want, bam = bam_paths, row.names = NULL),
          file.path(OUT, "PDO_sample_to_bam_map.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(lib, file.path(OUT, "PDO_library_sizes.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

cat("\nDone. Saved", nrow(sel), "genes x", length(want), "samples in:", OUT, "\n")
sessionInfo()
```
